sourced_facts: Eqs1-2 define a normalized Gibbs binary law with unary terms and an unrestricted function of total count.
Eq4 and page4 restrict recursive cardinality subsets to nested or disjoint sets; arbitrary potentials at their counts include unary factors.
Eqs6-7 introduce deterministic sum-count auxiliary variables without changing the binary law.
§5.2 messages are exact convolutions; §5.2.3 states O(D log² D) time and O(D log D) space for balanced FFT trees, with O(D²) worst-case time for unbalanced trees.
§5.3 samples root counts then child count splits and leaves to draw exact joint configurations.
new_primary_conclusions.overlap: Structured count supervision, proper count-dependent joint binary laws and exact marginal/sampling inference are established.
new_primary_conclusions.proposal_adaptation: Use a visible-context conditional two-sided count potential over native NCNC residual slots and label-only TRAIN observation bits; serve structural draws through one shared nonlinear decoder.
new_primary_conclusions.complexity_boundary: Arbitrary cross-side g(K_L,K_R) is not a unary potential on a single union count. It requires the separately stated full count-grid work; the paper fast bound is not claimed for that model.

sourced_facts: §3 trains a graph denoising network with per-variable classification losses on a noisy categorical graph.
The reverse step factorizes over nodes/edges conditional on the current noisy graph; that next graph is fed back through repeated learned transitions.
Shared graph-transformer context combines node, edge and global features; dense layers have quadratic node-pair work.
§4.2 and Appendix B add noisy/visible-graph structural and spectral descriptors; Appendix B notes cubic spectral work on the small graphs used there.
new_primary_conclusions.overlap: Joint structural generation, shared global graph context and structural augmentation are prior even when step losses are per-edge classification.
new_primary_conclusions.comparison_boundary: F is explicitly factorial conditional on the current NCNC context; the word BCE alone does not prove that every entire graph model is factorial.
new_primary_conclusions.proposal_adaptation: Use nonlinear all-slot/all-pair context from permitted NCNC inputs; do not import true-target graph descriptors or unqualified dense whole-Collab diffusion.

closest_duplicate_risk.ingredient: Finite mixture of factorial Bernoullis with component-wide likelihood and responsibility gradients. This ingredient is attributed prior, not the proposed novelty.

broader_retained_overlap: SGDiff joint subgraph density for LP
